entries.heading: Step 1 - Equipment endpoint: empty JSON result
explanation: The browser opens http://127.0.0.1:5085/api/v1/equipment and displays the JSON response []. This records direct browser access to the equipment-list endpoint.
The empty array means that this API response contains no equipment items. It is the expected list representation for an empty result, rather than an equipment object or a connection-error message.

This screenshot does not display the HTTP status code, the PostgreSQL database name, or whether the Desktop process is closed. Those points need separate terminal/database/process evidence; they are not inferred from this image.

For the walkthrough after the seven-item controlled dataset has been prepared, capture an additional populated equipment response. Retain this image as supplemental empty-result evidence rather than labeling it as the seven-item seeded catalog.
entries.scope: Supporting API-01 / Step 1 evidence only. No complete T01 or T07 pass is established by this image.

entries.heading: Step 2 - Register a student and verify the database row
explanation: The Students screen displays Demo Student with institutional number ST-UI-600 and contact demo.student@example.edu. The message "Student registered and eligible to borrow" confirms the registration result shown by the application.

The pgAdmin query filters the Students table by ST-UI-600. Its result contains one matching row with Id 1 and IsEligibleToBorrow set to true. The application also labels this student "Eligible to borrow", matching the database value.
This captures a registered student and a database readback of the matching identity. The displayed eligibility is the state after registration; no eligibility-change action is shown in this picture.
entries.scope: Student registration and matching database readback; HTTP request/response details are not visible.

entries.heading: Step 2 - Update student details and verify the same identity
explanation: The selected student now has the name Demo edited Student. The institutional number remains ST-UI-600, and the application displays "Student details saved".

The pgAdmin result shows one matching row with the same Id 1 and institutional number, with the updated name visible in the FullName column. Comparing this picture with Figure 2 supports that the existing student was updated while retaining the same database identity.

The contact field still contains demo.student@example.edu. These pictures demonstrate registration and a name edit; clearing the optional contact field is not demonstrated. If contact clearing is part of the walkthrough, add a separate screenshot showing a blank contact field and a database NULL result.
entries.scope: Student name update and retained identity. Contact clearing and persistence after a process restart are not shown.

entries.heading: Step 3 - Equipment registered in the management screen
explanation: The management list contains Demo Camera (EQ-UI-600), Demo Tripod (EQ-UI-601), Demo Microphone (EQ-UI-602) and Demo Tablet (EQ-UI-603). All four items are displayed as Available.

The screen explains that availability is read-only here and is controlled by borrowing and returns. The blank form is ready for a new item; the following database screenshot supplies the saved identifiers and descriptions.
entries.scope: Equipment management evidence; screenshots do not show HTTP exchanges or establish the full Lab 5 acceptance result.

entries.heading: Step 3 - Database readback before editing the camera
explanation: The SELECT query returns four equipment records with identifiers EQ-UI-600 through EQ-UI-603 and database Id values 1 through 4. All four IsAvailable values are true.

Before the edit, the camera has Id 1, name Demo Camera and description Demonstration camera. The tablet description is Zero-history control; that label alone does not prove an empty borrowing history.
entries.scope: Equipment management evidence; screenshots do not show HTTP exchanges or establish the full Lab 5 acceptance result.

entries.heading: Step 3 - Camera name edited and optional description cleared
explanation: The selected EQ-UI-600 item is now named Demo edited Camera. The description field is blank and the application reports Equipment details saved.
The camera remains Available, and the management page still states that availability is read-only. The next screenshot verifies the saved name and NULL description in PostgreSQL.
entries.scope: Equipment management evidence; screenshots do not show HTTP exchanges or establish the full Lab 5 acceptance result.

entries.heading: Step 3 - Database readback after the camera edit
explanation: The camera still has database Id 1 and identifier EQ-UI-600. Its name is now Demo edited Camera, its Description is NULL, and IsAvailable remains true.

Comparing the before and after results shows that the existing camera identity was retained while its name and optional description changed. The other three equipment records retain their displayed names, descriptions and available status.

These four pictures are consistent with the Step 3 equipment checks. The capitalization in Demo edited Camera differs slightly from the guide example but is consistent between the application and database. The separate ST-UI-603 / Demo Empty Student control registration is not visible in these images.
